releases.summary: Integrated the three August 6 lecture transcripts into respiratory control, respiratory system stressors, and air quality, with revised objective briefs and eleven transcript-grounded activities.
notes: Respiratory control now reflects the delivered emphasis on CO2-driven ventilation, the approximately 60 mmHg hypoxic threshold, central and peripheral chemoreceptor mechanisms, protective lung receptors, and major brainstem centers.
Stressors content now incorporates the instructor’s exercise scope, diving and altitude mechanisms, chronic adaptations, high-altitude illness distinctions, and treatment priorities.

Air-quality content now emphasizes occupation clues, chronic exposure latency, four priority outdoor pollutants, particle-size deposition, indoor radon/biomass risks, and race-neutral spirometry prediction.

Three future lecture groups remain marked Slides Only until their transcripts are available; anion-gap content remains outside the current MD827 assessment scope and supplied equations must be applied rather than memorized.

releases.summary: Integrated the three August 5 lecture transcripts into oxygen and carbon-dioxide transport, hypoxemia and hypercapnia, and arterial blood gas interpretation, with revised objective briefs and eight transcript-grounded activities.
notes: Oxygen content, hemoglobin-affinity shifts, CO2 transport, and the distinction among PaO2, SaO2, and CaO2 now reflect the delivered lecture emphasis.
The hypoxemia decision framework now emphasizes blood-flow-weighted V/Q summation, A–a gradient patterns, oxygen responsiveness, and the inverse relationship between alveolar ventilation and PaCO2.
ABG content now incorporates the instructor’s conceptual acid-base method, the 7.40/40/24 anchors, age-adjusted A–a interpretation, and worked clinical cases.
Six future lecture groups remain marked Slides Only until their transcripts are available.

releases.summary: Reordered all lecture content and learning objectives into the chronological Exam 1 schedule, beginning with the August 3 sessions and continuing through August 7.
notes: Objective Map, Study Library, lecture selectors, progress tables, reset controls, and Content Status now follow the canonical date-and-schedule sequence from the course schedule.
Learning objectives follow their original numbered order within each lecture; no question, rationale, or stable progress identifier was changed.
Today’s Plan remains adaptive and may intentionally deviate from chronology when due retrieval, misconceptions, or exam urgency take priority.

releases.summary: Integrated five August 4 lecture transcripts into four lecture groups, revised all 16 associated objective briefs, and added eight transcript-grounded retrieval activities.
notes: Airway resistance, dead-space, spirometry, respiratory mechanics, pulmonary circulation, and gas-exchange emphasis now reflects the delivered lectures.
Explicit instructor scope statements were preserved, including spirometry exclusions and the calculations expected for FEV1/FVC and the A–a gradient.
Nine future lecture groups remain marked Slides Only until their transcripts are available.
